$doc: Source's appearance, as data — the source of the `@component source` block in css/components.css and of dist/react/source.tsx. Same contract as components/button/definition.json: a plain string is a structural literal, {"token": "x"} binds --x, and an array is a sequence of both. SOURCE IS THE BLOCK THAT MADE A PART A FULL RULE. `.source__link` carries a hover-and-focus state and its canonical HTML puts it on a <button> and an <a>, so a part that could hold neither was a limit of the emitter rather than a fact about components. It also has two paragraphs — the list's own chrome, then the item that repeats inside it — which is a statement about which rules belong together and is recorded rather than lost. Six parts and no variants: nothing here has an axis, which is the line that still separates a part from a component of its own.

block.title: Source (citations)
note: Every claim traced to the passage it came from. An id reaches this
list only after the provenance gate has confirmed a tool actually
returned it this turn, so the list is a record, not a bibliography.

parts.name: title
parts.$doc: The word Sources. The mono chrome label at the floor of the type ramp — the same family and case as a chip, a fact title and a plate label, at its own step of the tracking ramp.

parts.name: list
parts.$doc: The <ol>. `counter-reset: none` is deliberate and is the one declaration here that exists to cancel something: the ordinal is drawn by `.source__ref`, so the list's own numbering would be a second, disagreeing count.

parts.name: item
parts.$doc: One citation. Baseline-aligned rather than centred, because the ordinal, the link and the id are three different sizes and it is the text they share that should line up.

parts.name: ref
parts.$doc: The ordinal, in a square. Its width and height are equal and literal because it is a box drawn around one or two characters, not a step on the spacing ramp — a rhythm token here would make the square follow the page's rhythm instead of its own type.

parts.name: link
parts.$doc: The citation itself. It is a <button> when it opens the passage in place and an <a> when it navigates, which is why the generated component is polymorphic — the canonical HTML shows both, and the emitter reads the element from there rather than being told.

states.name: engaged
states.$doc: One rule under two selectors: a pointer and a keyboard should land on the same appearance, and writing that twice would be the same CSS with a second place to forget.

parts.name: id
parts.$doc: The chunk id, shown so a claim can be traced by hand. `word-break: break-all` and `min-width: 0` are the pair that stops a long id from widening the flex row past its container.
